I am a 45-year-old woman farming 5 mu in Quzhou County. My husband and I have worked this land for 25 years, and our son works in a factory in Shijiazhuang, sending some money home. My daughter-in-law also helps when she is not working at the garment workshop. We grow wheat in winter and maize in summer on all 5 mu — that is what everyone around here does, and it keeps us fed.

**Winter wheat:** I will plant wheat around October 10th, after the National Day holiday. My son might come home to help for a day. I use the seed I saved from last year — it is a good variety I bought from the county supply store three years ago. Saved seed costs almost nothing, just some medicine to treat it before sowing. I put down about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that is two 50-kg bags for the whole 5 mu. I buy the fertilizer from the village cooperative. At Qingming Festival, when the wheat starts jointing, I topdress with about 10 kg of urea per mu — one bag total. My neighbor Li Sao does about the same, and she gets good yields, so I follow her. I irrigate three times: once in late November before the freeze, once at jointing in March or April, and once at grain filling in May. Water costs money now — the well is metered — so I do not waste it. I spray herbicide once in early spring for weeds. My husband and I do all the work except harvest, when we hire two people for two days because we need to get the wheat out fast before the rain comes. I expect about 420 kg per mu if the weather is normal. Last year we got 410, so 420 is reasonable.

**Summer maize:** The day after we finish wheat harvest in early June, we plant maize. The window is very tight — sometimes only three or four days. We usually do light rotary tillage or just plant directly if we are running late. Maize seed I always buy new — hybrid seed from the county store, usually Zhengdan or Yudan brand. It costs about 50 yuan per mu. You cannot save hybrid seed, it does not work the next year. I put compound fertilizer down at planting, about 20 kg per mu. I do not usually topdress maize unless the leaves turn yellow, then I might add a handful of urea, but usually the base fertilizer is enough. I irrigate once or twice — definitely at the big trumpet stage in July, and maybe at filling in August if there is no rain. Last year it rained enough, so I only irrigated once. I spray herbicide once after emergence. Maize is less work than wheat. My family handles it all — no hired labor needed. Harvest is in late September. I expect about 480 kg per mu.

**Money:** I am careful with cash. The factory sent less work last month, so my son's remittance was smaller. I have about 2,000 yuan for farm inputs this season. Fertilizer is the biggest cost, then maize seed and irrigation. I would like to put more fertilizer on, but I need to keep some cash for my grandson's school fees and for medicine if someone gets sick. I would rather apply a little too much fertilizer than too little — a bad yield means we eat less, but wasting some fertilizer is better than going hungry.
